pr_title: Fix amcrest detection of sensor reset
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Previous versions of pyamcrest passed a boolean to home assistant
depending on whether the event was the activation of a sensor or not.
This was used by the amcrest integration to decide the state of the
binary sensors.

The latest pyamcrest passes through a non-empty payload dictionary
instead, which is a true-value and the binary sensor would always
be deemed active.

Look into the payload for an "action": "start" item instead.

issue_context.title: Amcrest camera motion sensor state not getting reset in 2021.5
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have two Amcrest cameras.  After updating to 2021.5, the binary motion sensor state no longer changes to off once motion is no longer detected.  The sensor state correctly changes to on when motion is detected and then stays on forever.  Restarting Home Assistant will reset the state to off.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.5.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.4.6

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

Amcrest

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/amcrest/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
amcrest:
  - host: xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx
    username: !secret amcrest_username
    password: !secret amcrest_password
    name: Front
    stream_source: rtsp
    resolution: low
    binary_sensors:
      - motion_detected
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

2021.5.0:
```
2021-05-07 08:01:11 DEBUG (Amcrest Front) [homeassistant.components.amcrest] Sending signal: 'amcrest_event_Front_VideoMotion': {'Code': 'VideoMotion', 'action': 'Start', 'index': '0', 'data': {'RegionName': '['}}
2021-05-07 08:01:11 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.amcrest.binary_sensor] Updating Front Motion Detected binary sensor
2021-05-07 08:01:22 DEBUG (Amcrest Front) [homeassistant.components.amcrest] Sending signal: 'amcrest_event_Front_VideoMotion': {'Code': 'VideoMotion', 'action': 'Stop', 'index': '0', 'data': {'RegionName': '['}}
2021-05-07 08:01:22 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.amcrest.binary_sensor] Updating Front Motion Detected binary sensor
```

2021.4.6:
```
2021-05-07 08:19:32 DEBUG (Amcrest Rear) [homeassistant.components.amcrest] Sending signal: 'amcrest_event_Rear_VideoMotion': True
2021-05-07 08:19:32 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.amcrest.binary_sensor] Updating Rear Motion Detected binary sensor
2021-05-07 08:19:52 DEBUG (Amcrest Rear) [homeassistant.components.amcrest] Sending signal: 'amcrest_event_Rear_VideoMotion': False
2021-05-07 08:19:52 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.amcrest.binary_sensor] Updating Rear Motion Detected binary sensor
```

### Additional information

_No response_
comments: if you rollback does it fix the issue? wonder if this was caused by #49004
I rolled back to 2021.4.6 and it works.  I updated the original post with debug log info for both versions.
@FrnchFrgg any chance you can help out here?

Oh, I think I get it.

The problem is not due to the home assistant changes in #49004 but caused by the API change of pyamcrest, that we upgraded along with #49004. Before it mapped `Stop` actions to `False` and `Start` to `True`, and now it sends a dictionary with the event payload, but since it is not empty it is a `True`-like value from the integration's point of view.

That is an oversight, sorry. I'll submit a PR ASAP.

@joe248 can you try with 2021.5.0, but with the ` homeassistant/components/amcrest` directory (as it is in #50249) copied into your `custom_components` folder ? That way the patched version will override the faulty one.

If it is not too much hassle of course. I cannot test myself since my device does not produce these events.
@FrnchFrgg sure I can do that, but there's currently a few build errors on #50249.
@FrnchFrgg just tested your change and it's working again.  Thanks for the quick fix!

review_comments: Why the casting to lowercase? I would not assume an API to return random casing of keys and values. Is there more than one expected value?

Something like this should work, no?

```suggestion
                    start = payload.get('action') == 'start'
```

If `action` always exist, use the square brackets.
```suggestion
                    start = payload['action'] == 'start'
```
No, because the case does not seem consistent across devices. That's what the `lower()` are for.

That the payload syntax and content are *very* inconsistent across devices is a fact. But looking back at the old `python-amcrest` code, it looks like it searched explicitly for the string `action=Start` in the payload. Nowadays it sanitizes the payload (which can be `;`-separated, or `|` or `,` with or without quotes, with `=` or `:`, depending on the device) but seems to keep the key and value cases unchanged throughout.

So we can either go for my code, and try to support more devices, or go with the straightforward `start = payload.get('action') == 'Start'` that is exactly backwards-compatible.
For sure `"action" in payload` is not guaranteed.
